steps.name: Get Jira/Requirements
steps.description: Fetch the requirements from Jira, or take them from the prompt, and save them as-is.
steps.prompt: If the input is a Jira key, use the Atlassian MCP (getJiraIssue) to fetch the issue. If the input is free text, use it as the requirements. If there is no input, ask the user for a Jira key or a description. Write the requirements as-is to ./docs/sdlc/<slug>/requirements.md, then summarise them back to the user and confirm they are correct before moving on.

steps.name: Intent
steps.description: Interview the user to capture the intent behind the requirements, in their own words, as a version-controlled artifact.
steps.prompt: Use the $grill-with-docs skill to capture the intent behind the requirements. Write the captured intent to ./docs/sdlc/<slug>/intent.md. Summarise the intent back to the user and repeat until the user says 'approved'.

steps.name: Design
steps.description: Design the solution with the user, write the spec, and produce the implementation plan.
steps.prompt: Using the intent from the Intent step, run the $brainstorming skill to design the solution. Respect its approval gate. Write the spec to ./docs/sdlc/<slug>/spec.md (this path overrides the skill's default spec location). If brainstorming hands off to $writing-plans, save the implementation plan to ./docs/sdlc/<slug>/plan.md; otherwise write a short plan there yourself. Do not create a second plan document anywhere else. Commit the docs on the current branch (no worktree exists yet). Then score plan.md against the $karpathy-guidelines skill on a scale of 1-10 per guideline (Think Before Coding, Simplicity First, Surgical Changes, Goal-Driven Execution) with a one-line reason each. If the average is below 8, tell the user what to improve, revise the plan, and re-score. Repeat until the average is 8 or higher or the user says 'approved'.

steps.name: Sync to Jira
steps.description: Create or update Jira issues for the plan tasks: one standalone issue, or a parent issue with subtasks.
steps.prompt: First read ./docs/sdlc/<slug>/STATUS.md. If it already lists Jira keys for this run, update those issues (editJiraIssue) to match the current plan instead of creating new ones; only create issues for plan tasks that have no key yet. Otherwise use the Atlassian MCP (createJiraIssue) to sync every task in the plan to Jira. If the original input is a Jira key, reuse that issue as the parent and create one subtask for each plan task; if that parent is Closed or Done, ask the user before creating anything. Otherwise, if the plan contains exactly one task, create one standalone Jira issue and do not create a parent. If the plan contains multiple tasks, create one parent Jira issue from the requirements, then create one subtask for each plan task. Record every created or updated key, with its plan task, in STATUS.md.

steps.name: Build
steps.description: Implement the approved plan in an isolated worktree, one task at a time, with tests first.
steps.prompt: Use the $using-git-worktrees skill to create an isolated worktree and feature branch for this run. Record in ./docs/sdlc/<slug>/STATUS.md before writing any code: base branch, base commit SHA, worktree path, and feature branch name. Based on the complexity of the task, suggest which LLM models fit to use for code and tests and ask the user to confirm before delegating via the Task tool. Then use the $subagent-driven-development skill to implement the tasks in ./docs/sdlc/<slug>/plan.md in order, following $test-driven-development, with exactly one commit per task. Record the final HEAD SHA and test result in STATUS.md.

steps.name: Local Review
steps.description: Review the implementation against the repo's standards and against the spec to ensure both are correct.
steps.prompt: Use the $code-review skill. Fixed point: the base branch recorded in STATUS.md by the Build step. Spec: ./docs/sdlc/<slug>/spec.md. Report the Standards and Spec findings side by side. For each finding, ask the user whether to fix it now, defer it, or dismiss it; fix approved items in the worktree and commit.

steps.name: Push & Open PR
steps.description: Push the feature branch, open a pull request against the base branch, and keep it merge-ready.
steps.prompt: Push the feature branch recorded in STATUS.md to origin. Open a pull request against the base branch recorded in STATUS.md; use the spec summary as the PR description and link the Jira keys from the Sync to Jira step. Record the PR URL in STATUS.md. Then use the $babysit skill until the PR is merge-ready. Do not merge.
